relevance.rationale: A survey of the motivic fundamental group of the projective line minus three points and its relation to multiple zeta values: Belyi's theorem and the faithful Galois action on the profinite fundamental group, the pro-unipotent completion and its mixed-Tate-motive structures, motivic periods, and the motivic Galois group acting on them. The corpus makes exactly these moves in prose with no citations at all: rem:transcendental-accounting asserts that the depth-3 Bring periods Li_3(zeta_5^k) span a 4-dimensional Q-vector space on which S_5 acts irreducibly and that 'their post-archimedean structure is governed by the motivic Galois group, not by the q-rational pre-image', and rem:vol-as-motivic-period asserts each Bloch-Wigner value D(z_i) is a Kontsevich-Zagier period — both blocks contain zero \cite. There is also a registered q-deformed multiple-polylogarithm reference whose own scope note warns that it supplies no q-analogue of the {0,1,infinity} picture and points at an open bean; this survey is the classical side of exactly that picture. Supporting rather than core: it is a review, it supplies the framework and vocabulary the corpus's period claims presuppose, but no single theorem here is consumed by a derivation.

keyResults.locator: sections 1-1.1 (Belyi's theorem; Deligne's pro-unipotent completion and its motivic structures)
keyResults.statement: The pro-unipotent completion of the fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity} carries the structures of a mixed Tate motive over Z, and its periods are the multiple zeta values, on which the motivic Galois group acts.
keyResults.useForFolio: The citable framework for rem:transcendental-accounting's 'governed by the motivic Galois group' claim and rem:vol-as-motivic-period's Kontsevich-Zagier period claim, both currently uncited.

proposedActions.rationale: Relevant, no ref() entry, and the corpus has no reference at all for motivic periods / mixed Tate motives despite two blocks reasoning with them.
rem:transcendental-accounting and rem:vol-as-motivic-period both invoke motivic periods and the motivic Galois group with no citation whatsoever; this survey is the standard entry point.
